policy_title: Regenerate Britain's defence manufacturing and technology
stated: Reform UK will introduce incentives and tax breaks to boost the UK defence industry, improve equipment self-sufficiency, and manufacture world-class products for export.

source.quote: Regenerate Britain’s Defence Manufacturing and Technology Introduce incentives and tax breaks to boost the UK defence industry. Improve equipment selfsufficiency and manufacture world class products for export.

bearing_set.reason: Improving equipment self-sufficiency and defence manufacturing capacity directly bears on national security resilience and the UK's defence posture — a real verdict on the safety & security fundamental.

Tax breaks and incentives targeted at defence manufacturing would plausibly affect job creation, job quality, and pay in a high-skilled industrial sector — a non-negligible verdict on good work & fair pay.

Tax breaks and incentives targeted at defence manufacturing constitute an industrial policy with concrete effects on business investment, productivity, and export-led economic opportunity — core O13 indicators.

Named tax breaks and incentives reduce government revenue; unless fully offset by growth in corporation and income-tax receipts (contested), they widen the deficit — a specific O12 mechanism against the 'is spending funded vs borrowed' indicator.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the defensive/security effect (O5), the industrial-growth effect (O13), and the fiscal cost of the tax-break instrument (O12). Business tax breaks do not directly shift household take-home pay so O11 does not clear the bar; O4 job-quality effects are real but secondary and subsumed within the aggregate O13 analysis at this level of policy specificity.
